numbers.bench_density_limit: **The density test could act only on 268 of 309 searched held-out stars,** those whose TOI-table entry gives both log g and R★.
numbers.bench_stellar_sentence: The benchmark runs did not query the TIC: each star's parameters came from the TOI table's own columns (Teff, log g, R★). Limb darkening used Teff and log g (the Sun's values where missing; Teff was published for 306 of 309 searched held-out stars), and ρ★ was computed from log g and R★, so the density test could act only on the 268 stars with both.
numbers.cmp_pht_note: With 9 stars in the 3 to 4 R⊕ bin the interval cannot tell the two apart.
numbers.cmp_pht_sentence: 3 to 4 R⊕, consistent with Planet Hunters TESS's rate; above 4 R⊕, significantly below Planet Hunters TESS's rate
numbers.code_fingerprints: `14f6f4830a525d78` = commit 76de67d (HEAD differs only in comments and docstrings); `e4fe4c99663ccba8` = commit 40cceca (HEAD differs only in comments and docstrings)
numbers.feed_half_sentence: Noise alone would account for 0.82 of that rate, at least half, so a `new_candidate` on the feed is more likely noise than a signal.
numbers.floor_meaning: On this benchmark J therefore mostly measures how separable false positives are from catalogue metadata, not how well a method reads light curves.
numbers.lb_subsample_overlap: every pair of their completeness intervals overlaps
